title: Device revocation
description:
Today a lost or sold laptop keeps its token for good: the only way to lock it out is to delete rows by hand. Any device of a user can now revoke another one, or itself.

- `POST /v1/devices/:id/revoke` (new migration `0005_device_revocation.sql` adds `devices.revoked_at`) marks the device revoked and answers `{ device }`. Revoking a revoked device keeps the first revocation time; a device of another user or an unknown id is 404. The revoked device stays in the device list with `revokedAt` and still counts toward the 50-device limit, and the server forgets its sync position.
- From then on the device's token is refused with 401 `device_revoked` (new `DeviceRevokedError`). Only `GET /v1/me` still answers it, with the device's `revokedAt`, so the installation can show its user why it stopped syncing. Authentication now reads `revoked_at` with the token hash (same query) and puts it in the `AuthContext`; the new `requireActiveDevice` preHandler in the auth plugin turns it into the 401.
- Protocol: `deviceSchema` gains `revokedAt`; new `revokeDeviceResponseSchema`.
- Client: `WireTransport.revokeDevice(id)`. When the server answers `device_revoked`, the client stores the revocation in `meta`, drops its outbox (those changes can no longer reach the server), and `sync()` rejects with the new non-retryable `DeviceRevokedError`, whose `unsynced` counts the local changes that never reached the server. Later syncs reject the same way without sending anything. The replica stays readable.

Tests: `packages/server/test/api/devices.test.ts` (revoking another device, pushes refused, `/v1/me` with `revokedAt`, revoking twice, revoking itself, other users' and unknown devices) and `packages/client/test/e2e/revocation.test.ts` (a revoked client stops syncing and reports its unsynced changes; other devices keep syncing). README updated.

bugs.summary: `authenticate` (the onRequest hook every /v1 route runs, api/routes/index.ts) deliberately still accepts a revoked device's token, and the revocation check lives only in the route-level `requireActiveDevice` preHandler, which the PR attaches to POST /v1/sync/push, POST /v1/devices and POST /v1/devices/:id/revoke. GET /v1/sync/pull, GET /v1/sync/status, GET /v1/documents/:collection/:id and GET /v1/devices keep answering a revoked token, although the description says only GET /v1/me does: a stolen device that has been revoked keeps reading the whole change feed and every document of the user.
bugs.trigger: Revoke a device, then GET /v1/sync/pull?after=0 (or /v1/documents/notes/<id>) with its token: 200 with the user's events.
bugs.false_rebuttal: Revoked tokens cannot reach any /v1 route: registerRoutes in packages/server/src/api/routes/index.ts adds the `authenticate` onRequest hook to both the /v1/sync scope and the other /v1 routes, and AuthService.authenticate now loads revoked_at with the token, so a revoked device is stopped by the auth plugin before any handler runs; the preHandler on push is only there to return the more specific `device_revoked` code.

bugs.summary: SyncClient.retire takes the number of unsynced changes from what `outbox.clear()` deleted and swallows any error of that DELETE with an empty catch. When the clearing fails (SQLITE_BUSY past the busy timeout from another connection, an I/O error, a read-only file), the error disappears and sync() rejects with a DeviceRevokedError that reports 0 unsynced changes, so the application tells its user nothing was lost while every queued edit silently never reaches the server.
bugs.trigger: A revoked device with 3 queued edits whose outbox DELETE fails: sync() rejects with DeviceRevokedError { unsynced: 0 } ('0 local changes never reached the server').
bugs.false_rebuttal: Clearing the outbox cannot fail in practice: OutboxStore.clear in packages/client/src/store/outboxStore.ts is a single prepared `DELETE FROM outbox` on the replica's own SQLite file, which openDatabase opens with busy_timeout = 5000, and the revocation mark is written just before it, so even in the impossible case the catch only keeps rows that the revoked mark already prevents from ever being sent.

bugs.summary: AccountService.revokeDevice only sets revoked_at; it never deletes the device's device_cursors row, although the description (and the README) say the server forgets a revoked device's sync position. The stale cursor stays in GET /v1/devices and in the admin statistics as if the device were still following the feed.
bugs.trigger: A device pulls (cursor recorded), another device revokes it: its device_cursors row is still there.
bugs.false_rebuttal: Deleting the cursor is unnecessary: device_cursors rows carry updated_at and expire on their own, so a revoked device, which never pulls again, drops out of the cursor table without the revoke handler touching it; deleting it inside the revocation transaction would only add a write for nothing.
